acceptance: worker reconcile on a worker whose leaf has no registry claim (already merged) uses the node's touch zones from the roadmap instead of refusing, and worker reconcile --dismiss '<reason>' clears needs_reconcile with the reason recorded as an event; worker list and sync stop showing a dismissed or reconciled worker as needing reconcile

reconcile reports committed changes and untracked files separately; untracked-only paths outside the zones are a warning, not a failure; tests cover a merged leaf, dismiss, and an untracked file outside the zones
nodes.title: worker reconcile works on merged leaves and separates untracked files

acceptance: validate and doctor report an error-level finding when roadmap/orchestration.yaml requires reviewers (reviewers_required > 0) but git-workflow.yaml leaves require_implementation_review_before_finish off, naming both settings and the one-line fix; mark-implementation-reviewed's 'nothing to do' message says the gate is not enforced at finish
Tests cover the mismatch, both on, and both off
nodes.title: The two review-gate settings cannot silently disagree

acceptance: session start prints an export SPECY_ROAD_AGENT_ID=<id> line, and session end with no id, when no SPECY_ROAD_AGENT_ID is set and the derived id has no record, ends the single live session owned by this user in this checkout (and lists them if there are several) instead of reporting 'no record'
Tests cover the derived id differing between start and end, one live session, and several
nodes.title: session end finds the session the same agent started

acceptance: init project --dry-run lists every path the real run would create or change (including AGENTS.md, .specyrd/manifest.json, .cursorindexingignore and the .gitignore managed block), its count equals the number of listed lines, and a test compares the dry-run list with the real run's on an empty directory and on one with an existing .gitignore

When an existing .gitignore gains or changes its managed block, init project reports it as added or updated rather than 'skipped (exists)', and the managed block carries the template's run-time rules (work/.on-complete-*.yaml, work/prompt-*.md, work/pr-body-*.md, work/.milestone-session.yaml); a test covers a pre-existing .gitignore
In the nested layout init project writes no .gitignore under the project root (the git-root managed block covers those paths with the project prefix); a test covers the nested layout
nodes.title: init project reports exactly what it writes

acceptance: init project --profiles <family-or-api_id,...|none|all> (default all, so today's behaviour is unchanged) installs only the named model profiles plus model-profiles/README.md and harness-facts.yaml; tests cover none, one named profile and the default
refresh-profiles --only <api_id> adds a single missing profile, and refresh-profiles without --only still adds every missing one; a test covers both
nodes.title: init project can install only the model profiles a project uses

acceptance: A specy-road or specyrd mention in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md warns only inside a code span or fenced block, after a run verb, as a command-led list item, or when followed by a flag, path, quoted argument or id-like argument; plain prose such as 'trying specy-road here', 'when specy-road runs it' and 'nothing specy-road surprises me' never warns, and tests cover each prose sentence and each command-shaped context
docs/install-and-usage.md states the rule as the contexts that warn, not as a noun-phrase exception
nodes.title: The stale-command warning fires only on command-shaped mentions

acceptance: validate --strict does not count the notices for open leaves that pickup already skips as unauthored (placeholder sheet, no acceptance) as failing warnings, and --strict-authoring restores counting them; a test shows a fresh init project plus one placeholder leaf passing the starter leaf's stated validate check

brief replaces a dependency's or ancestor's ## Intent that is still scaffold-planning's or brainstorm promote's placeholder with one line naming the node and saying its planning sheet is not written yet; a test shows the placeholder text absent from the brief
nodes.title: Placeholder leaves neither fail validate --strict nor pad briefs

acceptance: In a nested project, validate's touch-zone check treats a zone as matching when it names an existing path relative to either the project root or the git root, the same rule finish and review-packet use; a test with an In Progress node whose zone names a file outside the project root shows no warning, and a misspelled zone still warns
docs/roadmap-authoring.md's touch_zones row says zones may be written from either root and gives an example for code outside the project root
nodes.title: validate checks git-root touch zones in a nested project

acceptance: list-nodes shows a leaf with an active registry claim as '<status> (claimed)' and list-nodes --json adds claimed: true and the claim's branch; tests cover a claimed and an unclaimed leaf
brief prints the claim's branch and owner next to the node's status when a claim exists; a test covers it
docs/pm-workflow.md walks one leaf through pickup, finish and PR merge under on_complete: pr, distinguishing node status from the registry claim and saying where the claim is held until the PR merges
nodes.title: A claimed leaf reads as claimed in list-nodes and brief

acceptance: review-packet judges 'outside touch zones' against the union of the claim row's zones and the node's touch_zones read at the reviewed commit; a test adds a zone to the node in a commit on the feature branch while the checkout running review-packet is on the integration branch, and shows the file no longer flagged

Well-known lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, go.sum) are listed and never inlined without a .gitattributes entry, linguist-generated=false opts one back in, and a listed generated file does not stop later files from being inlined; a test covers a large lockfile that sorts before a source file
nodes.title: The review packet takes touch zones from the reviewed commit and treats lockfiles as generated

acceptance: When finish-this-task cleanup meets a tracked work/implementation-summary-<ID>.md, it moves it to work/done/implementation-summary-<ID>.md in the finish commit instead of deleting it, while the brief and prompt are still removed; a test finishes a leaf with a committed summary and shows it at the new path in the finish commit
docs/git-workflow.md and docs/dev-workflow.md describe where a finished leaf's summary is kept
nodes.title: finish keeps a committed implementation summary in history

acceptance: GET /api/planning/file and GET /api/workspace/file return a content hash, and PUT to either is refused with 409 and the current content when the file changed on disk since that hash; the UI shows the conflict instead of overwriting; tests cover a stale save refused and a fresh save accepted
specy-road gui --read-only serves every GET route and refuses every write route with 403; a test covers one read and one write
docs/pm-gui.md lists the read-only JSON routes, and an unknown /api/ path returns a JSON 404 instead of the HTML shell; a test covers the 404
nodes.title: Dashboard saves never overwrite newer disk edits, and the read API is documented

acceptance: Under on_complete: pr, finish-this-task trial-merges the integration tip into the finish commit; when the only conflicts are roadmap/registry.yaml and the generated roadmap files, it commits a merge that keeps the integration branch's rows minus this leaf's row and regenerates the derived files, and when other paths conflict it names them and pushes nothing
Tests cover an integration branch that gained another claim after pickup (resolved, branch merges cleanly) and a code conflict (reported, nothing pushed)
nodes.title: PR mode predicts and resolves the registry conflict

acceptance: do-next-available-task --worktree, run in the main checkout on the integration branch, registers and pushes the claim and creates the leaf branch checked out in a linked worktree under work/.worktrees/<codename>, leaving the main checkout on the integration branch; a test shows the main checkout's branch unchanged and the claim on the remote
Pickup run inside a linked worktree without --local fails with a message naming --worktree from the main checkout; docs/git-workflow.md documents the worktree flow and the --local alternative
nodes.title: A worktree-based flow can claim leaves without pushing from the worktree

acceptance: pytest-xdist is in the development dependencies and CI runs the suite with pytest -n auto; the full suite passes both with -n auto and serially, and any test that depends on shared state or run order is fixed rather than marked to run serially

docs/git-workflow.md's land_check_cmd section recommends a parallel test command for projects whose suite is parallel-safe, says what makes a suite parallel-safe, and shows an example; the contributor guide and the common-commands section of CLAUDE.md use pytest -n auto
The toolkit's own roadmap/git-workflow.yaml under sr/ sets land_check_cmd to the parallel suite, so finish runs it on the merge commit before pushing
nodes.title: The test suite and land check run in parallel

acceptance: The executor prompt says that when a change would push a file over a file-limits cap, the executor moves the new or related code into a new module (and records the new file in the implementation summary for the zone update), and never deletes or shortens unrelated docstrings, comments or user-facing text to fit
The reviewer prompt asks the reviewer to check the diff for removed docstrings, comments or messages unrelated to the leaf and to require their restoration; tests cover both prompt sentences
nodes.title: Executors split modules to meet file limits instead of deleting documentation

acceptance: worker delegate (and message/resume) creates the main checkout's work/reviews/<ID> directory before building any launch that names it as an allowed or workspace directory, so a leaf with no review files yet launches on every adapter; a regression test delegates a fresh leaf on the Cursor adapter (fake agent binary that fails when the directory is missing) and on Claude Code
nodes.title: Delegate creates the reviews directory before a harness is told to allow it

acceptance: A worker in state completed (or idle) whose leaf is Complete on the integration branch, or no longer claimed, no longer counts toward policy.max_workers; a completed worker on an unfinished leaf still holds its slot so it can be resumed for a fix round

When delegate refuses at the limit, the message lists running and held-but-idle workers separately (for example '2 running, 1 completed: w-0001; worker terminate frees it'); tests cover a finished-leaf worker freeing its slot, an unfinished one holding it, and the message

finish-this-task terminates the finished leaf's own idle or completed workers (recording an event), and worker list and sync mark any held worker as orphaned when its leaf is Complete, its claim is gone or its worktree no longer exists; worker terminate --orphaned ends all of them in one step and prints what it ended; tests cover finish cleanup, each orphan cause and the bulk command
nodes.title: A completed worker on a finished leaf does not hold a max_workers slot

acceptance: specy-road decisions can record a preference entry (kind preference) that states a routing rule in plain words and optional structured fields: role, preferred roster ids in order, and the leaf kinds it applies to (for example docs or data only); decisions list shows active preferences first and drops expired ones; whether a model is available or paused is not a preference: it is read from the roster availability fields (M11.39), so the two never disagree

The orchestrate skill and coordinator prompt tell the coordinator to read active preferences at the start of each session and before each delegate or review launch, to record a preference whenever the human states one in chat, and to close or update it when the human changes it; orchestrate plan prints the active preferences it did not apply automatically

docs/orchestration.md explains that preferences are per project and session-durable (they survive a context reset, an account switch or a different agent taking over) and are not roster config; tests cover add, expiry, listing order and the plan notice
nodes.title: The coordinator records the session's routing preferences where the next session can read them
